stem:
A 67-year-old man with long-standing hypertension undergoes left heart catheterization with simultaneous phonocardiography and left ventricular pressure-volume recording. Immediately after the end of ejection, ventricular pressure falls rapidly while ventricular volume remains unchanged and no blood enters the ventricle. A sharp sound is recorded at the onset of this interval.

Which of the following valve events most directly produces this sound?

options.label: A
options.text: Simultaneous opening of all four heart valves
options.misconception: An impossible valve configuration is being proposed for a normal sound.
options.explanation: All four valves never open together in the normal cycle; the second heart sound is produced specifically by closure of the semilunar valves.

options.label: B
options.text: Closure of the mitral and tricuspid valves
options.misconception: The onset-of-systole atrioventricular closure is being credited with the post-ejection sound.
options.explanation: Mitral and tricuspid valve closure produces the first heart sound at the start of systole; the sound recorded after ejection ends reflects semilunar valve closure.

options.label: C
options.text: Closure of the aortic and pulmonary valves
options.misconception: None; semilunar valve closure marks the start of isovolumic relaxation and produces S2.
options.explanation: When ventricular pressure falls below arterial pressure at the end of systole, the semilunar valves close, producing the second heart sound and beginning isovolumic relaxation with all valves shut.

options.label: D
options.text: Opening of the atrioventricular valves during ventricular filling
options.misconception: A silent diastolic opening event is being substituted for an audible closure.
options.explanation: Atrioventricular valves open silently during diastole when atrial pressure exceeds ventricular pressure; the audible event after ejection is semilunar closure.

options.label: E
options.text: Opening of the semilunar valves at the start of ejection
options.misconception: The ejection-phase opening event is being placed at the post-ejection interval.
options.explanation: Semilunar valves open when ventricular pressure exceeds arterial pressure to begin ejection; the interval described follows ejection and ends with their closure.

context: Learning objective: link S2 to isovolumic relaxation. After ejection, falling ventricular pressure closes the semilunar valves (S2), then both valve sets remain shut during isovolumic relaxation before atrioventricular valves reopen for filling.
